correctness.rationale: The regularity double count gives the sharp universal lower bound. Equality forces pairwise matching symmetry by solving the exact closed-neighborhood equations. Explicit label-count constructions cover every nonexceptional admissible pair; the two exceptions have separate impossibility arguments for weights \(2k\) and \(2k+1\) and explicit weight-\(2k+2\) witnesses. Exhaustive direct-definition checks for \(n=3,4,5\) agree with the theorem, while the infinite conclusion rests on the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The theorem completely resolves a canonical graph family across the entire admissible \(k\)-range, characterizes every lower-bound equality structurally, and isolates exactly two exceptional pairs. It also shows that deleting a single perfect matching from the balanced complete bipartite graph changes the same invariant by two over a broad infinite range, giving a motivated perturbation phenomenon rather than an arbitrary finite computation.
